scope: Offline audit and visual review of a user-run original-PyTorch backward tracking diagnostic. No inference, builds, conversions, exports or benchmarks were run by the assistant.

run.controlMeaning: Same-input relabeled forward calls validate reverse indexing under the pinned settings. They do not establish subject identity or independent accuracy.
run.seedMeaning: A manually reviewed saved forward prediction at frame 375 is the mask prompt. A fresh pointer and memory are built from that mask and its source pixels; seed presence is forced by the native mask-input path, not measured identity confidence.

offlineChecks.attentionBudgetMeaning: One conditioning frame plus up to six recent spatial records and fifteen recent pointers; spatial records expand to 512 tokens each and pointers to four tokens each.

descriptivePresence.meaning: Presence counts are not correct-recovery counts. Masks can select the wrong person, include foreground distractors, or miss part of the target; empty/empty overlap is not a success.

visualReview.targetDescription: The selected man wearing a black graphic T-shirt and khaki shorts.

findings.observation: Backward is empty while saved forward retains genuine target partials at the left image edge. Full-resolution frame 165 confirms visible torso/arm omitted by backward.
Backward produces tiny lower-left fragments before forward resumes. Their identity is not established by presence; enlarged frame 191 is too limited to count as a clean recovery.
Both broadly follow the target shoe and partial body; exact boundaries remain imperfect.
Backward includes the foreground man's pointing hand/forearm along with the intended target. Enlarged frames 225 and 229 clearly show this added error, which forward avoids.
Backward is blank while forward retains tiny edge fragments; no per-pixel ground-truth claim.
Backward begins as a narrow strip near the foreground occluder's shoulder. The earliest strip is ambiguous and should not be counted as confirmed recovery.

Backward generally follows the reappearing intended man through a stretch where forward is blank except at 277. Enlarged frame 300 (10.0 s) clearly shows recovered target head/torso, with imperfect coverage including an omitted forearm. This is qualitative benefit, not 45 ground-truth-correct masks.
Both are empty despite a visible target sliver. Agreement on absence does not establish correctness.

Forward repeatedly selects a foreground hand and later mixes the target with the blonde foreground woman's hair/shoulder. Backward is blank at 343-344 and then generally follows target head/hair/visible body instead. Enlarged 346, 354 and 360 show a substantial improvement; boundaries are not asserted perfect.
Both broadly select the intended man with coverage differences.
Exact agreement is by construction from the saved forward mask prompt, not independent validation.

interpretation.conclusion: A manually seeded backward pass provides useful complementary target masks on this development clip, but is not a global replacement for forward tracking.
rejectedInferences: All additional nonempty backward frames are correct recoveries.
Passing reverse-index controls validates subject identity.
Backward is always preferable, or union/intersection can safely fuse the masks.
The effect isolates direction alone: later initialization and temporal evidence change jointly.
Two agreeing passes provide independent evidence; the later seed is itself a forward prediction.
This original-PyTorch CPU result establishes Core ML reverse support, device performance, or held-out accuracy.
interpretation.nextDirection: Use saved forward/backward disagreement examples to design and evaluate a controlled segment-selection or user-review approach. Preserve genuine partials as well as rejecting wrong foreground masks. No automatic selection rule or acceptance threshold has been established.
